business.summary: Deepak Nitrite operates primarily across two key segments: Phenolics and Advanced Intermediates, delivering chemical products for domestic and export markets with a domestic-to-export revenue mix of 86:14 in Q4 FY26. The company is actively expanding its manufacturing capabilities into downstream products such as MIBK, MIBC, BPA, and Polycarbonate, while accelerating transition towards renewable energy.

promises.promise: Accelerating transition towards green energy by sourcing 60% to 70% of energy mix from hybrid renewable sources
promises.delivered: Long-term horizon; progress on exact percentage mix not specified in subsequent documents.

promises.promise: Commissioning of multipurpose agrochemical intermediates, MIBK, and MIBC projects scheduled in Q2 FY27
promises.delivered: In Q1 FY27 concall, management confirmed MIBK, MIBC, and acetophenone scheduled to be commissioned in August itself with rest within Q2 FY27; later in Q2 FY27 concall, management noted 'with all the assets that have been commissioned running at steady-state'.

promises.promise: Polycarbonate project expected to be commissioned by June 2028
promises.delivered: Reiterated in Q1 FY27 concall with target around H2 FY28-29; horizon of June 2028 has not arrived.

promises.promise: MIBK as well as MIBC commissioned along with acetophenone in August itself, and the rest within Q2
promises.delivered: By Q2 FY27 concall, management referenced all assets commissioned and running at steady-state.

promises.promise: Capex spend of around another INR 1,000 crore to INR 1,500 crore in FY27
promises.delivered: FY27 is ongoing as of Q2 FY27; net debt stood at INR 1,657 crore in Q2 FY27. Final full year FY27 spend pending.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Consolidated total revenue for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 1,983 crore, growing 3% YoY and QoQ.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Table reports Dec 2025 (Q3 FY26) Sales of Rs 1,975 crore, reflecting +4% YoY growth (vs Rs 1,903 crore in Dec 2024) and +3.8% QoQ growth (vs Rs 1,902 crore in Sep 2025).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Consolidated revenues for Q4 FY26 stood at INR 2,127 crore with EBITDA at INR 383 crore and PAT at INR 220 crore.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Table shows Mar 2026 (Q4 FY26) Sales of Rs 2,120 crore, Operating Profit of Rs 376 crore, and Net Profit of Rs 220 crore.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 improved 35% YoY and PAT reached INR 345 crore, registering 207% YoY growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Table reports Jun 2026 (Q1 FY27) Sales of Rs 2,578 crore (+36% YoY vs Rs 1,890 crore in Jun 2025) and Net Profit of Rs 345 crore (+208% YoY vs Rs 112 crore in Jun 2025).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 reached INR 3,091 crore with 61% YoY growth, and EBITDA reached Rs 643 crore with 21% margin.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Table reports Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27) Sales of Rs 3,076 crore (+62% YoY vs Rs 1,902 crore in Sep 2025), Operating Profit of Rs 627 crore, and OPM of 20%.

guidance.guide: Targeting commissioning a couple of months after Polycarbonate in FY28-29
Spend around another INR 1,000 crore to INR 1,500 crore in FY27
Targeting about 14% to 15% EBIT next year with commissioned assets running at steady-state

bull: Revenue growth accelerated sharply from -3% YoY in Mar 2026 to +36% in Jun 2026 (Rs 2,578 crore) and +62% in Sep 2026 (Rs 3,076 crore), driven by record Phenolics performance.
Operating profitability has expanded significantly, with OPM rising from 9-11% during FY26 to 21% in Jun 2026 and 20% in Sep 2026, delivering Rs 627 crore of Operating Profit in Sep 2026.
Net Profit reached an all-time high of Rs 398 crore (EPS of Rs 29.16) in Sep 2026 compared to Rs 119 crore (EPS Rs 8.70) in Sep 2025, while net debt-to-equity improved to 0.25x in Q2 FY27.
bear: Interest expense has increased steadily, rising from Rs 6 crore in Dec 2024 to Rs 29 crore in Sep 2026, alongside depreciation rising to Rs 71 crore.
High domestic concentration risks remain, with the domestic to export revenue mix standing at 86:14 in Q4 FY26.
Substantial ongoing capex commitments (INR 1,000 to 1,500 crore in FY27, plus Polycarbonate and BPA projects out to FY28-29) maintain execution and commissioning risk.
